mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior month's level, accompanied by a decline in CPIAUCSL, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to tightened policy expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >70% of triggered events, or the policy shift is not confirmed by subsequent market pricing (SPX 1-month implied volatility does not rise).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PAYEMS (labor market activity) above the 50th percentile of its 12-month rolling distribution predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as hiring momentum supports corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: Rank IC for this signal < 0.05 over the 60-day horizon in >80% of instances, or SPX 20-day returns are negative despite the labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 2% predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as a leading indicator of weakening manufacturing demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prev(INDPRO) AND INDPRO < INDPRO[1m ago]
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns are positive in >50% of such INDPRO declines, or the decline is not followed by a persistent S&P 500 drop.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) rises by more than 10% month-over-month, it signals renewed confidence in the housing market, which amplifies equity risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in 95% of such events, or HOUST growth is not confirmed by SPX options flow (put-call ratio).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS below 2% and UNRATE above 6.5%), a sharp drop in RSAFS (money supply growth) of over 1% in a month predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as a sign of excess liquidity.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND UNRATE > 6.5% AND RSAFS < prev(RSAFS) AND (RSAFS - prev(RSAFS)) / prev(RSAFS) < -0.01
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns remain positive in >60% of such RSAFS drops, or liquidity conditions revert before the 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 5% for three consecutive months predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as labor market tightness supports corporate hiring and productivity.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0 AND UNRATE > UNRATE[1m ago] AND UNRATE > UNRATE[2m ago]
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such UNRATE trends, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in GDPC1 (real GDP) of at least 2% forecast a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as a leading indicator of economic weakness and reduced consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < prev(GDPC1) AND GDPC1 < GDPC1[1m ago] AND (GDPC1 - prev(GDPC1)) / prev(GDPC1) < -0.02
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of such GDP declines, or GDP weakness is not followed by S&P 500 underperformance.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains unchanged for two consecutive months while CPIAUCSL rises by 0.5% or more, it signals a shift toward inflation targeting and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to market uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS == prev(FEDFUNDS) AND CPIAUCSL > prev(CPIAUCSL) AND (CPIAUCSL - prev(CPIAUCSL)) / prev(CPIAUCSL) > 0.005
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >70% of such events, or FED policy signals are not confirmed by market pricing (SPX volatility does not rise).
